directAnswer: To mirror a Mac screen, use the AirPlay feature to connect to an Apple TV or compatible device. Ensure both devices are on the same Wi-Fi network.
summary: Mirroring your Mac screen can enhance presentations or allow for larger viewing experiences. This guide outlines the steps to achieve screen mirroring using AirPlay.

sections.heading: Setting Up AirPlay
sections.body: Ensure your Mac and the device you want to mirror to (like an Apple TV) are connected to the same Wi-Fi network. Click the AirPlay icon in the menu bar to see available devices.

sections.heading: Adjusting Display Settings
sections.body: Once connected, you can adjust display settings by going to System Preferences > Displays. Here, you can choose to mirror or extend your display.

steps.title: Enable AirPlay
steps.detail: Click the AirPlay icon in the menu bar at the top-right of your screen and select the device you want to mirror to.

steps.title: Choose Display Mode
steps.detail: Select 'Mirror Display' to show the same content on both your Mac and the external display.

steps.title: Adjust Resolution
steps.detail: Go to System Preferences > Displays to adjust the resolution and scaling options if needed.

faqs.question: What if the AirPlay icon is not visible?
faqs.answer: If the AirPlay icon is missing, ensure your Mac supports AirPlay and is connected to the same Wi-Fi network as the receiving device.

faqs.question: Can I mirror to multiple devices?
faqs.answer: No, AirPlay only allows mirroring to one device at a time. You can switch between devices, but not mirror to multiple simultaneously.

faqs.question: Is there a way to mirror without AirPlay?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can use a physical HDMI cable to connect your Mac directly to a monitor or TV for mirroring.

caveats: Mirroring performance may vary based on network speed and distance from the router.
